newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates up, spots mostly down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates up, spots mostly down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up on Thursday due to a new issue on the Shenzhen A share market on Friday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rose to 12.99 percent from 11.94 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover fell to 9.53 million lots from 9.72 million lot. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The offer of Liaohe Tongda Chemical Co tomorrow on the Shenzhen bourse triggered some big institutions to get funds," one trader said.
Rises in the domestic A share markets in both Shenzhen and Shanghai were another important factor pulling the early-maturing contracts up, traders said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down due to a technical correction after rises in the past week, trader said.
The most active ten-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 117.21 yuan from 117.60 yuan on Tuesday. Turnover of the bond fell to 430 million yuan from 1.13 billion.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 637,606 lots from 1.53 million lots.
"Technical charts showed the spots have started a technical correction after the continous rises since Wednesday of last week," one trader said.
But traders said they expected a rumour that the central bank would cut bank interest rates in the first quarter of 1997 would support prices in the next few days.

"The spots are likely to move into an upward channel in the first half of 1997 due to the fall in domestic inflation and expected lower coupon rates of T-bills to be issued in 1997," a second trader said.
